<reason>CON won a competitive debate by pinning the motion on an operating rule, not a moral claim: “close to standard” secretly purchases nearby specialized density. That matching problem stayed live after mixed dispatch, fleet replacement, and “some reserve capacity.” PRO was strong on exclusion, accountability, and absolute floors that can still leave large gaps, but never showed how 12-versus-10 waits arrive without idle coverage or cannibalizing edges—especially after saying every car need not be converted. CON’s alternative (floors, ramps, procurement) gave a cleaner vote against this specific mandate.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Q1 on sedan-like pickup without idle oversupply; PRO answered with a larger dual-use fleet, then CON used the 12-vs-10 standard and edge-cut concession to show “close” still ranks density over honest scarcity.</best_rebuttal>
